chunks: And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Saffan ibn Yahya, from one who narrated to him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Like it.
And he said: 'It is not permissible for him to pray the two rak'ahs of the obligatory Tawaf except behind the Maqam, due to the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious:
And take you the station of Ibrahim as a place of Salat (prayer).'
So if you pray them in any other place, then upon you is the re-prayer of the Salat.'

key_terms.رَكْعَتَيْ طَوَافِ الْفَرِيضَةِ: The two rak'ahs of prayer following the obligatory circumambulation (Tawaf)

ai.seo_question: Where must the two rak'ahs of Tawaf prayer be performed according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) via Safwan ibn Yahya, emphasizing the strict requirement to pray the two rak'ahs of Tawaf specifically behind the Maqam Ibrahim. This directive is grounded in the Quranic command to 'take the Station of Ibrahim as a place of prayer,' and the Imam clarifies that praying elsewhere invalidates the prayer, necessitating repetition. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on literal adherence to the specific location mentioned in the Quranic text for ritual validity.
